Black Friday is still a few months away, but you don't have to wait that long to score some great deals on gaming peripherals that can instantly up your game. Starting now and running through September 27, SCUF is kicking off its aptly named It's Time to Win Sale with up to 20% off performance gaming controllers for every platform. Premium controllers usually command a premium price point, and SCUF is no exception, with its top-end controllers priced upwards of $200. That's why you don't want to miss out on any opportunity to get one on sale. The SCUF "It's Time to Win" Sale Is Live: Save Up to 20% Off SCUF's "It's Time to Win" sale is a bit different from the previous Labor Day Sale we saw earlier this month. For starters, SCUF's top-of-the-line Omega PlayStation controller is now part of the sale. Also, instead of just the standard editions being discounted, SCUF's more uniquely designed offerings are also marked down as well. These include the pre-customized Design series, the collaborative Creator series, and the completely customized build-your-own Builders series controllers. Prices are as marked and no coupon code is required. The sale cannot be combined with other discounts, pending or existing orders, and is not applicable on gift card purchases. The Omega Is the Ultimate PlayStation 5 Controller The officially licensed SCUF Omega PlayStation 5 controller is, frankly, what the DualSense Edge should have been. It adopts the DualSense's familiar layout with dual analog sticks and iconic geometric face buttons, but just about every component has been upgraded. For starters, both analog sticks are equipped with SCUF's Endurance TMR sensors. TMR joysticks are a step up from Hall Effect. Although both use electromagnetic technology with no moving parts and thus are highly resistant to stick drift, TMR joysticks offer finer control, higher precision, and are more power efficient. They also cost more to manufacture, so they're only found in top-grade controllers. The D-pad and face buttons are equipped with clicky Omron mechanical switches which provide satisfying tactile feedback. The L2/R2 triggers are dual action with two separate trigger stops. With a flip of a switch, you can choose between a short-throw "mouse-click fast" action or the more standard full-throw action. There are also six additional buttons - four rear paddle switches and two side buttons (exclusive to SCUF) - that can be depressed without your thumbs ever leaving the thumbsticks. As if that still wasn't enough inputs, five "G-Keys" are positioned along the bottom edge of the controller, with two of the keys being programmable via the SCUF mobile app. Note that this controller is also compatible with PC. The VALOR PRO Wireless Is SCUF's Best Xbox Controller The VALOR PRO Wireless is SCUF's best pro controller for Xbox. The front-facing layout mirrors the tried and true Xbox asymmetrical control scheme with XY/AB face buttons. Much like the Omega, this officially licensed Xbox controller has pretty much every available feature to wipe out the competition including SCUF's Endurance TMR joysticks, Omron mechanical switches, dual action L/R triggers, and rear paddle switches. It lacks the side-mounted buttons and G-keys of the Omega, but the VALOR PRO does uniquely feature tri-mode connectivity (wireless, wired, and Bluetooth) alongside Corsair's low latency SlipStream technology. Note that this controller is also compatible with PC. The VALOR PRO Wired TMR Is an Outstanding Value If you do not need wireless connectivity, then the VALOR PRO's wired TMR value will save you loads of money. It retails for $99.99 but currently on sale for $89.99. This controller is identical in design and features to the wireless version except for, obviously, the lack of tri-mode connectivity (since there's no wireless or Bluetooth option). Instead, the controller connects to your Xbox or PC via a detachable USB Type-C cable. Many old school gamers still swear by wired connectivity since it eliminates any input lag concerns, and this controller is perfect for them. The Envision Pro V2 Is Exclusive to PC Gamers Both the Omega and Valor Pro are PC compatible, but SCUF carries one more wireless PC controller that's a bit more affordable. The Envision Pro V2 looks more like an Xbox than the PS5 controller because of the XY/AB face buttons, but it adopts technologies from both. The joysticks are equipped with Hall Effect magnetic sensors, not quite as precise as TMR but a big upgrade over traditional potentiometer-based analog sensors. Like the rest of the lineup, the Envision Pro V2 features Omron mechanical switches, dual action triggers, and the four rear paddle switches. Carried over from the Omega are the two side buttons and five G-keys. In fact, all of the G-keys are programmable (as opposed to just two on the Omega). Carried over from the Valor Pro is Corsair's low latency SlipStream technology. items.title: Love Nikki Player Shuts Down Fan Website Over Game's 'Irreverent' and 'Demonic' Clothing Designs
items.excerpt: A fan of the Love Nikki – Dress Up Queen mobile dress-up game is going viral for shutting down their informative website after determining that some of the game’s clothing designs were “demonic.”
items.content_text: A fan of the Love Nikki – Dress Up Queen mobile dress-up game is going viral for shutting down their informative website after determining that some of the game’s clothing designs were “demonic.” Nikki’s Info was a fan-made website compiling many of Love Nikki’s clothes, accessories, story guides, update details, and other information. An X/Twitter account for the site was created in 2018, and players could subscribe to the administrator’s Patreon for exclusive game guides and other insights. Those players are now being offered refunds after the site’s admin announced that they are quitting the game due to their religious beliefs, as described in a now-viral blog post . The admin published the post after a week of inactivity on the Nikki’s Info website, which has been completely wiped of any information relating to the dress-up game. They explained their absence in the post, saying they had “done some horrible things involving the occult” and that the “devil had then gained such a foothold in my life [that] I was firmly in his grasp.” “All of this started quite small and personal — but quickly escalated, where in the end I was in a situation where I was in a near-death situation involving police, paramedics, and other people, of whose kindness I am grateful for. I [was] on the precipice of a terrible situation — [I] called out to God for help. He answered. I then continued to practice the occult. Things got worse again and started affecting others, especially my suffering family, in a way I can’t declare publicly,” they wrote. While the poster confirmed that they are now fine, they expressed some issues with the clothing designs in Love Nikki, finding them to be blasphemous with “demonic” undertones. “The game features a lot of crosses as dress-up items, which are irreverent to God, the God who so kindly and patiently saved me. The God I love,” they continued. “There’s a lot of them, disproportionately so. Some are mixed in with gothic demonic themes. Such things, though they might seem small, carry consequences and meaning. This is not to say that playing the game directly led to what happened to me. I can say with some degree of certainty, it really was the terrible things I did. But in the ‘back story,’ the various games, books, works of fiction, movies, even music — they are there. “I have wrestled with this, but ultimately I can’t profit from or promote something which offends my God, my Saviour — therefore the site is now closed. The source code, the data, the domain are not for sale.” ⭐Behind the Seams | [Version 2.0 5-Star Outfits] The Inspirations Behind the Designs pic.twitter.com/KMOoKqvo67 — Infinity Nikki (@InfinityNikkiEN) December 10, 2025 The admin’s post has gone viral within the broader Infinity Nikki community, sparking concerns from players and theories as to what clothing items specifically led them to this conclusion. Some pointed out the oddness of the situation, given that a fair few designs within the Nikki franchise were directly inspired by figures within the Catholic religion. For example, Love Nikki includes an outfit set that’s essentially a Pope-like ensemble, while the official Infinity Nikki X account shared a graphic with specific details about how the team at Infold approached its Behind Prayers outfit set, saying the Starlight Crown headdress incorporated “imagery of the Virgin Mary.” For now, commenters are doing their best to help the Nikki’s Info admin, though the situation has sparked no end of curiosity and debate within the world of dress-up games.
